literature_notes: All nine ledger clips (L1–L9) describe a single class of construct: full-length human CD86 with GFP or mCherry fused to its C-terminus. L1 is the most explicit: 'GFP tagged to the C-terminus of CD86.' Computed topology places the CD86 C-terminus (residue 329) firmly in the intracellular domain (residues 269–329). The tagged protein is surface-displayed and functional (it supports CTLA-4-mediated transendocytosis), but the fluorescent tag itself faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular space. No ledger line describes an N-terminal extracellular insertion, an internal loop insertion, or any tag on the extracellular domain (residues 24–247). Because the sole evidence class is a cytoplasmic C-terminal fusion, zero extracellular surface tag sites are supported.

literature_other_positions.note: GFP fused to the C-terminus of full-length CD86; residue 329 (F) is intracellular (topology residues 269–329), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
